dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Infinite Graphs
dossier_meta.statement_text: Problem Does there exist a graph with no subgraph isomorphic to $ K_4 $ which cannot be expressed as a union of $ \aleph_0 $ triangle free graphs?
dossier_meta.context_text: Shelah [S] has proved that the existence of such a graph is consistent with ZFC.
dossier_meta.references_text:
- *[EH] P. Erdos and A. Hajnal, On decomposition of graphs, Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 18 (1967), 359–377.
- [S] S. Shelah, Consistency of positive partition theorems for graphs and models, in Set Theory and Applications, Springer Lecture Notes 1401, (Toronto, ON, 1987), 167–193.
